etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English scrowle, scrolle, from earlier scrowe, scrouwe (influenced by Middle English rolle), from Old French escroe, escrowe, escrouwe (“scroll, strip of parchment”), from Frankish *skrōda (“a shred”), from Proto-Germanic *skraudō, from *skrew- (“to cut; cutting tool”), extension of *(s)ker- (“to cut”). Doublet of shred and escrow.

definitions.definition: A roll of paper or parchment; a writing formed into a roll.
(architecture) An ornament formed of undulations giving off spirals or sprays, usually suggestive of plant form. Roman architectural ornament is largely of some scroll pattern.
Spirals or sprays in the shape of an actual plant.

quote.citation: 1985, Peter Balakian, “The Oriental Rug”, in Robert Pack, Jay Parini, editors, Introspections: American poets on one of their own poems, Hanover and London: University Press of New England for Middlebury College Press, published 1997, →ISBN, page 31:
quote.text: I lose myselfin a flawed henna plantjutting toward the scroll.Its rose-pink eyes burstoff the stems.

definitions.definition: A mark or flourish added to a person's signature, intended to represent a seal, and in some States allowed as a substitute for a seal. [U.S.] Alexander Mansfield Burrill.
(lutherie) The carved end of a violin, viola, cello or other stringed instrument, most commonly scroll-shaped but occasionally in the form of a human or animal head.
(cooking) A kind of sweet roll baked in a somewhat spiral shape.
(computer graphics) The incremental movement of graphics on a screen, removing one portion to show the next.

quote.citation: 2005, Alberto de Lózar Muñoz, Liquid Crystal Dynamics: Defects, Walls and Gels, page 1:
quote.text: […]  the computer sends orders, via electrical impulses, to recompose the liquid crystal structure inside the cells quickly which results in the familiar smooth scroll of the pointer on your screen.

definitions.definition: (hydraulics) A spiral waterway placed round a turbine to regulate the flow.
(transitive, computing, graphical user interface) To change one's view of data on a computer's display by moving in gradual increments, typically using a scroll bar or a scroll wheel..
(intransitive) To move in or out of view horizontally or vertically.

quote.citation: 2017, Patricia Taxxon (lyrics and music), “Player Piano”, in Black and White:
quote.text: The piano plays on. I watch those little rectangles as they  scroll down from the top.

quote.citation: 2018, Darrin Doyle, Scoundrels Among Us: Stories:
quote.text: Pavement scrolled beneath the headlight beams, reminding Emma of a conveyor belt.

definitions.definition: (Internet, intransitive, dated) To flood a chat system with numerous lines of text, causing legitimate messages to scroll out of view before they can be read.

quote.text: It's cool but i know why I prefer newsgroups : I just got banned for scrolling or summat : i was typing one word in each message so pppl[sic] could read it cos it was going so fast - geez.

quote.text: If you want to join this riot, we urge you to!     You wont have to worry about being TOSed or reported because there will be no Guides online!   So do whatever you want—punt, scroll, tos, just turn AOL into a war zone!
